questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I work in the art world and my dream is to combine the studies of art history and French culture studies. Paris is a historical centrum, so I saw it as an incredible possibility to go and study in the center of it all. The courses offered at the Sorbonne fit my study plans perfectly. In Paris I could study the culture and then visit it after class. 
The language aspect was also very important; to improve my French as much as possible by living with a French host.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was a hard puzzle to get all the classes/schedule set up. There was not much help with that. 
The courses were incredible, but the grading was very strict based on the fact that I am an Erasmus student. The classes were very hard to pass even though I worked so hard.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was hard I general to get information on scheduling and classes or cancelation of classes. Some teachers used the online platforms and some didn't. It was a solo project - but I made it work! 
Parismus worked very well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I received a date to go and pick up my university card and one e-mail with a zoom introduction to the faculty. 
It took a lot of work to plan out the classes in the different locations (many different Sorbonne buildings around town). Mostly help from other erasmus students, and then by learning the French way over time. 
Every teacher introduced every class and the plan for the semester during the first week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Mentioned in boxes further up.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Through personal contacts from growing up abroad in Bruxelles. 

I recommend living with a French host to be able to practice as much French as possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
it can be more lonely than living with fellow students. Socializing can be a bit harder. 
But it makes you use the language you came to learn. And living locally is an amazing experience,

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was offered a Sorbonne student housing space, but I had already found one privately.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Not much help or guidance accessible. Very slow e-mail responce from French university. 
Most help came from other students or experience.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
One short introduction to all the erasmus/parismus events at the Sorbonne - where I also received my student id and got my arrival note signed. 
One zoom meeting about how to create your schedule and apply to classes. 
a great Walk-in meeting at the art history faculté to sign up for the right classes. 
Other classes was done through e-mail and in person in class when giving the e-mail address.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Zoom meeting in the beginning. 
E-mails to the eramus coordinators.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I got all the classes I wanted, but it was very difficult to create the schedule. The buildings are scattered all over the city, so it was a bit difficult to create before testing it out. I chose to take classes in two different facultés - if I would redo it, I would chose one over two. 
I struggled getting the right info and dates for assignments on multiples classes. 
It was just a very different system.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Chose one faculté. 
test out the distance between buildings first.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The art history program was everything and more. The courses at the literary departement was also very interesting, but I was lacking a lot of background knowledge expected in these courses - elements from past semesters. 
I truly enjoy the way "TD/CM" work; the grand lectures followed by smaller classes with room for details. 
The way the courses are set up is very logical, chronological and made sense for me who grew up in Belgian schoolsystem. A lot of info, but it makes sense. 
negative; a lot of student presentations in the TD, almost whole classes were dedicated to the mandatory presentations. I would rather have listened to the professor. ^

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
If I wasn't a student of French culture and language back home, I would have found it very hard to understand context. But I am and it was great to see how well  my danish education prepared me in terms of culural and historic context. 
 The courses at the literary departement were also very interesting, but I was lacking a lot of background knowledge expected in these courses - elements thought during past semesters. I had a hard time understanding the assignment form - the work we had to hand in was very different than the danish forms. 
Forms / formats that the French have been learning since le lycée.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I truly enjoy the way "TD/CM" work; the grand lectures followed by smaller classes with room for details. 
The way the courses are set up is very logical, chronological and made sense for me who grew up in Belgian schoolsystem. A lot of info, but it makes sense. It was clear and logic.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *

Shopping in supermarket was less expensive - more possibilities. 
high rent and expensive navigo card. 
Amazing free acces to museums ass a student in Paris.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Not much info on that or time for it. 
A couple movie nights organized by school. 
Parismsus organises a lot of parties and walking tours  for erasmus students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Jobs trough studies. 
Shared uni coffeshops and friday-bars. 
many other groups and theme nights organized at uni.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
A lot of museums have free entrance for students and classes at Bozart. 
I recommend to go and participate and meet some erasmus students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go and see some art. 
Walk around Paris.
Join the Erasmus events during the daytime. 
Ask questions about the schools assignment forms ; they are very strict and different, other requirements.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I speak fluent French, so it was easy to live as a local.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
It was hard to meet locals. the classes are not connected, so every class has new students and no breaks to socialize. 
The students are very young, they usually don't take gap years + they already know each other from high school. It takes a lot of work to enter the French circles.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Paris is a very private and intense city - many people on the go. It can almost be to easy to be lonely in Paris. You have to follow the Parisian flow and walk very fast.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I enjoy the French culture and language very much. 
I like the politness and respect in dialogues with strangers.
My favorite thing about France is the appreciation towards art and the history/ culture of their country. In France you don't question if art is important or not. The past and spoken words exists everywhere from metro stop names to presidential speeches.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Save up a good sum of money before going. Apply for legater.
Do not only prioritize school over social life - socializing and having people around is very important.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Practice the local language as much as possible. 
when handing in assignments; The format is more important than the content. The format is very strict and decides your whole grade. 
Have a good French/cultural historic overview before.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The art courses and the city experience. The flow of the city - the fact that there's always something to do in Paris. 
Studying in the most beautiful places and historic buildings. Studying art in a place that celebrates it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The grading of the papers. I worked hours and hours on them but received very low grades even though I speak fluent French. 
The format is more important than the content.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: More guidance in the beginning of the semester would have been good. Especially some help with finding all the course overviews etc.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
